objective.statement: Learn six more performance words and what they ask the player to do.
successCriteria: I know andantino, prestissimo and tempo primo are about speed.
I know espressivo, sostenuto and con moto are about the way to play.
I can match each word with its meaning, in words or on a melody.

explanation.text: Music is full of Italian words that say how to play. Here are six new ones. Three are about speed and three are about the character of the music.
Andantino means a little faster than andante, the walking pace you know. Prestissimo means as fast as possible: faster than presto. Tempo primo means return to the speed at the start.
Espressivo means expressively, with feeling. Sostenuto means sustained: the notes are held on and supported. Con moto means with movement, so the music keeps moving forward.
These words are usually written above the stave at the start of a piece or a section. Always check whether a word describes speed, loudness, the touch of the notes or the mood.
Speed words only compare with other speed words. Andantino and prestissimo are not opposites of each other: one is a gentle walking pace, one is the fastest of all.
Speed: andantino, prestissimo, tempo primo. Character: espressivo, sostenuto, con moto.

music.textAlternative: A two-bar melody in G major marked espressivo.

steps: Look at the word above the first bar: espressivo.
It describes the character: play with feeling.
It does not change the speed: only the way you shape the notes.
demonstration.textAlternative: A short melody in G major with the word espressivo above the first bar.
